message.content:
Nicolaus Copernicus faced criticism from clerical authorities who feared the heliocentric model challenged Scripture.  
Aristotelian philosophers objected because a moving Earth contradicted everyday experience and established natural philosophy.  
Astronomers such as Georg von Ebers dismissed his system for relying on assumptions without sufficient mathematical evidence.  
Did the Church officially condemn Copernicus during his lifetime?  
Why did many scholars resist a universe in which the Earth was not the center?  
How could the motion of the Earth be reconciled with the observations available at the time?  
How astonishing it was that a quiet reformer dared to challenge ancient cosmology!  
What a striking challenge his work De Revolutionibus presented to medieval worldviews!  
How bold a declaration this was for one man!
